papers.title: Extending a property of vector spaces to abelian groups
papers.abstract: In this note, we determine the finite abelian groups $G$ such that for every subgroup $H\leq G$ there exists an automorphism $f\in{\rm Aut}(G)$ with ${\rm Fix}(f)=H$. This provides a partial answer to a problem posed by Deaconescu and Walls. Two generalizations of this problem are also proposed.

papers.title: A positive answer to Barsotti and Carman's question on unit groups of Burnside rings of fusion systems
papers.abstract: Let F be a saturated fusion system on a finite 2-group S, and let B(F) be the Burnside ring of F. Barsotti and Carman proved that when S is abelian, B(F)^*=B(S)^* if and only if F=F_S(S). Barsotti and Carman asked on page 728 of their paper whether there exists a counterexample to Corollary 9.3 for a nonabelian 2-group. We have given a positive answer. Our main conclusion is that the following are equivalent for all finite 2-groups: (1)F=F_S(S); (2)B(F)^*=B(S)^*; (3)For every maximal subgroup M of S, 1-[S/M] is in B(F)^*.

papers.title: Dense Exact Factorizations of Countable Topological Groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every countably infinite group endowed with a topology of countable weight in which every nonempty open set is infinite admits an exact factorization into two dense infinite subsets. More generally, every finite partial exact factorization with nonempty factors extends to an exact factorization of the whole group in which both factors meet every member of a prescribed at most countable family of infinite subsets in infinitely many points. This settles the countable case of a question of Protasov and Slobodianiuk. The proof uses the finite graph Ramsey theorem, invariant finitely additive probability measures on amenable groups, and a structural lemma on quadratic coverings based on Neumann's coset covering lemma.

papers.title: A Note on the OpenAI Construction of Counterexamples to the Kaplansky Direct-Finiteness Conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a human-readable exposition of OpenAI's construction of a group algebra in characteristic two that is not directly finite. We then adapt the argument to show that, for every prime $p$, there exists a hyperbolic group $G_p$ such that $\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$ is not directly finite.

papers.title: Steinberg module and top-dimensional cohomology for arithmetic Chevalley groups
papers.abstract: We prove that for a Chevalley--Demazure group scheme $\mathcal{G}$ of type $G_2$, $F_4$ or $E_8$ and a Euclidean ring $\mathcal{O}$ with field of fractions $K$, the Steinberg module of $\mathcal{G}(K)$ is generated by integral apartment classes. As a consequence, the top-dimensional rational cohomology of $\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{O})$ vanishes if $\mathcal{O}$ is a ring of integers, extending results of T\'oth and of Br\"uck--Santos Rego--Sroka.

papers.title: On supersoluble like groups of automorphisms of compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a not necessary full automorphism group of a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. We found sharp bounds for $|G|$ in the terms of $g$ when $G$ belongs to one of the following classes of finite groups sharing similar properties with supersoluble groups: 2-nilpotent, with the Sylow tower of supersoluble type, with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal cyclic primary subgroups, widely supersoluble, with submodular Sylow subgroups, with submodular cyclic primary subgroups and strongly supersoluble.

papers.title: Distinguishing invariants of Cayley Graphs, Hamming graphs, and wreath product actions
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a nontrivial group that acts on a graph $G=(V,E)$. The total distinguishing number $D''_{\Gamma}(V\cup E)$ (distinguishing index $D'_{\Gamma}(E)$) of the action is the least number of labels required for a total labeling (edge labeling) of $G$ so that the only elements of $\Gamma$ that preserve the labeling belong to the pointwise stabilizer of $V\cup E$ (pointwise stabilizer of $E$). We obtain upper bounds of these invariants for Cayley graphs and under various group actions, including free actions, wreath product actions, and coordinatewise actions on Cartesian powers of graphs. Our first main result shows that, if $\Gamma$ acts faithfully on $G$, with $|V|\geq 2, |E|\geq 1$ and the natural action of the wreath product $W=\Gamma\wr S_k$ on $V^k$ induces an action of $W$ on the Cartesian power $G^{k}=(V^{k},E_k)$, then $ D''_{W}(V^k\cup E_k)\le D''_{\Gamma}(V\cup E)+k-1 $ for any $k\geq 2$. We also establish the sharpness of several of our bounds through examples involving cyclic, symmetric, and alternating groups. Moreover, we determine these distinguishing invariants for the symmetric group action on Hamming graphs.

papers.title: Averages of sub-additive functions through non-Følner sequences
papers.abstract: We study the quantity $\sup_{\phi\in\Phi}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\phi(F_n)/|F_n|$, where $\mathcal F= (F_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of finite subsets of a countable amenable group, and $\Phi$ is a collection of subadditive functions. Under mild conditions on $\Phi$ we prove that the aforementioned quantity equals the supremum over $\phi\in\Phi$ of the limit of $\phi(F)/|F|$ as $F$ becomes more and more invariant, multiplied by a ``F{\o}lnerness'' constant $C(\mathcal F)\in[1,\infty]$. We have $C(\mathcal F)=1$ if and only if $\mathcal F$ is F\o lner. A corollary of this result is that every choice of a non-F\o lner sequence overestimates topological and measure-theoretic entropy by the multiplicative factor $C(\mathcal F)$ (in the positive entropy case). We obtain a generalization of classical results of Goodman, Krug, and Newton, on the so-called proportionality principle for sequence entropy, and their extension by Gao, Huang, and Zhu to countable amenable groups.

papers.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
papers.abstract: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.
